claims.text: The initial CoCrFeMnNi alloy has a homogeneous, single-phase FCC microstructure.
The initial CoCrFeMnNi alloy was synthesized by rapid solidification.
Intrinsic compositional complexity in CoCrFeMnNi facilitates nucleation of nanoscale chemically modulated ordered domains during tensile deformation.
Applied tensile stress perturbs local chemical equilibrium and triggers short-range atomic ordering within the FCC matrix.
The stress-induced ordered domains act as discrete barriers to dislocation motion.
Obstruction of dislocation motion by ordered domains causes localized strain accumulation.
Localized strain accumulation caused by the ordered domains triggers brittle crack initiation and premature toughness degradation.
Conventional-alloy embrittlement mechanisms primarily involve grain-boundary segregation or brittle grain-boundary precipitation.
Stress-induced ordering in the FCC matrix is distinct from conventional grain-boundary segregation and precipitation mechanisms.
The undeformed or low-stress baseline contains uniformly distributed elements and no detectable ordered domains.
Tensile-loaded specimens will develop ordered domains that correlate spatially or temporally with strain-localization zones.
Regions containing deformation-induced ordering will exhibit reduced ductility and lower fracture toughness relative to the homogeneous baseline.
Ordering-induced embrittlement will be most prominent at lower temperatures and strain rates for which dislocation mobility is limited.
Elevated temperature or conditions promoting homogeneous plastic flow will diminish ordering-induced embrittlement.
In situ synchrotron diffraction and TEM across room temperature to 500 K can be used to monitor ordering during incremental tensile loading.
Digital image correlation can map local strain evolution during uniaxial tensile testing.
Elevated temperature or slower strain rates are controls expected to suppress ordered-domain formation.
Absence of ordered domains concurrent with strain localization and brittle failure, or absence of a significant mechanical difference from baseline, would reject the proposed mechanism.
